sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden standing male figure with crested hairstyle, bored-hole eyes/nostrils, cloth waist wrap and fibre neck cord, attributed directly by the museum's production notes to the Irigwe (Kwoll) people — a clear example of their carved figure sculpture.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary studio/outdoor portrait of an Irigwe woman wearing traditional cloth wrap, wrist and neck ornaments, head-cloth, and visible scarification—consistent with the ethnographic record of dress and adornment.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: The photo shows a girl leaning on a mud granary with thatched huts behind, wearing a waist-cloth/ornament and carrying a child on her back — a documentary image of daily life and traditional dress plausible for the Irigwe region of Nigeria.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary portrait of an Irigwe woman wearing a head-cloth and neck-ornaments, with scarification visible on chest and shoulders — a clear depiction of traditional dress and body adornment of the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: A documentary portrait of an adult man identified as Irigwe, wearing a hat, hide shoulder strap, and wrist-ornaments while smoking a long ornate pipe — a clear ethnographic photo of dress and daily life matching the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary photo of a man wearing a hat and traditional attire crawling from the low entrance of a circular thatched-roof dwelling typical of Nigerian Plateau-region compounds, consistent with Irigwe daily life and architecture.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary photograph of women and children in traditional dress (head-cloth, leaf belts) beside a thatched granary/hut, consistent with Irigwe daily life in Nigeria; no evidence contradicting the claimed group.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary photo of a woman in traditional dress and ornaments standing before a decorated shrine building, consistent with Irigwe daily/ritual life in Nigeria; this is exactly the kind of photographic evidence of dress and material culture the criteria accept.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: The photo shows a man wearing a head-band and wrist ornament crawling out of the low circular entrance of a traditional thatched-roof dwelling, consistent with documentary photography of Irigwe daily life and vernacular architecture in Nigeria.

arms.name: dagger
arms.title: dagger
arms.reason: The image shows an iron dagger with a loop handle and incised geometric ornament, directly attributed to the Irigwe as maker — a weapon type consistent with Nigerian/Plateau region ironwork.

arms.name: dagger
arms.title: dagger
arms.reason: The image shows an iron knife with a wooden/leather-wrapped handle and a stamped leather tassel sheath, a type of edged weapon attributed by the museum to the Irigwe of Nigeria; this matches the claimed ethnicity and category.
